summary: A 1974 light at the end of the Leslie Street Spit, marking the Eastern Gap, where Department range lights and a fog alarm had stood since 1895.

access.note: Tommy Thompson Park is open on weekends and holidays, and weekdays 4 to 9 pm; private vehicles are not allowed; the light is about 4.8 km from the park entrance. Grounds open, tower closed.

events.note: Hexagonal tower marks the outer end of the Leslie Street Spit (Vicki Keith Point)
Light first shown from the 1974 tower
Eastern Gap range station established (Lighthouse Directory: station established 1895; front tower 1898, rear tower 1906)
Fog bell installed on the front range tower at the East gap, spring 1900
Diaphone fog alarm at the East gap, put in operation on the opening of navigation in 1905; building work by Jesse Tulloch
Fourth-order lens with occulting screen and petroleum-vapour light at the Eastern gap (report printed 1908)
Wooden dwelling for the fog alarm engineer built at the East gap station by contract, $3,295.78 (report printed 1910)

Eastern Gap range lights relocated to Humber Bay: one to the Mimico Cruising Club, one to the Etobicoke Yacht Club

notes_for_editor: The 1974 tower's shape and material disagree across sources (LighthouseFriends: hexagonal concrete; Lighthouse Directory: octagonal steel; Coast Guard: white hexagonal with red upper portion). Wikipedia says the 1974 light replaced the outer and inner pier lights on the East Gap 'from 1906' and that the towers went to Mimico and Etobicoke in 1981; no citable source says the 1974 tower replaced them, so the story does not say so and the links are not used. The Lighthouse Directory gives the range station's establishment as 1895, the front tower 1898 and the rear 1906; the Eastern Gap range towers were deactivated in 1973. The East Entrance records (ca-on-toronto-east-entrance-outer and -inner, the Mimico and Etobicoke towers) describe those relocated range towers, but their coordinates sit near longitude -79.48, about 9 km west of this station at -79.34: they are not the East Gap station. The East Gap fog alarm keeper George McKelvie (keeper statements of 1906 and 1910, wind gauge in 1912) is now in the roster with a caveat: he kept the same gap, but the sources do not say he kept this 1974 tower. Keeper statement rows are OCR tables: the 1910 row 'Toronto, East Gap | George McKelvie | June 13, 1905' and the 1906 row 'McKelvie, Geo | Eastern Gap Fog Alarm, Toronto' were checked on the page images (printed pp.171 and 165): each name sits on the same printed row as its station. The 1916 gale is the season of the fiscal 1916-17 report: the Director of the Toronto Observatory's report (printed p.242, checked in the volume text) gives the first warning as 21 April, the last as 6 December, and the heaviest general gale as 22 November; the year 1916 is inferred from the season. The 1912 gale's 40 mph maximum is not attributed to a station. The 1914 changes table lists 'Toronto, Eastern gap' beside a 4th order dioptric lens replacing a 6th order lens, but its OCR columns do not align with the station names, so it is not used. The 1905 fog alarm distance from the back range light is OCR'd as 'ttt mile' and is not used. No newspaper search was run for this station. LighthouseFriends gives the park name date as 1985 and the 1974 tower as concrete; neither is needed in the story.
